answer: Every identity locks a bond in the basalt registry with a receipt chained to its funding, exposing shared funders. The k-th identity from one funder costs k times the base bond: N clones cost roughly N squared bonds, a superlinear price no botnet can amortize. Each epoch every identity climbs to the summit checkpoint, a fresh sequential proof salted by its address and epoch, so one computation cannot serve many clones. The network also plants lantern canaries, honeypots posing as recruits; any identity vouching for one exposes its cluster, and the registry slashes every bond in it at once.
